A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GMOCP/EGMOCP work. All pages, including Appendices A and B, are readable, and retained algorithms, proofs, tables, and figures can be matched despite the changed title and formatting.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original experiments on CIFAR-10C, CIFAR-100C, TinyImageNet-C, and synthetic images.

after.justification: The original empirical evaluations are retained, with additional baseline comparisons, candidate-model controls, local-coverage measurements, and temporal analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and the graph sampling, model selection, adaptive miscoverage updates, and EGMOCP set-size feedback remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 substitutes set size into a theoretical argument; it does not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Table 10 adds an explicit CIFAR-10C evaluation under sudden distribution shifts; v1's reported CIFAR-10C evaluations use gradual shifts. The underlying datasets and classification tasks are retained, including TinyImageNet-C and synthetic data already present in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates the multi-model baselines MOCP and COMA. V2 adds ACI, FACI, DECAY, and SAOCP in Table 7, each with high-, medium-, and low-performance model configurations, substantially broadening the comparison to single-model methods.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a control using six high-performance candidate models (Table 8) and local coverage over 100-observation windows (Table 9). Table 7 specifies fixed GMOCP and EGMOCP configurations for the added baseline comparison. Existing training budgets, score functions, and principal evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices B.6–B.8 add tests of performance when candidate models have similar quality, short-window coverage under abrupt shifts, and prediction-set fluctuations across 6,000 timesteps. These substantially extend v1's model-count variations and DenseNet quality illustration with additional robustness and temporal diagnostics.

E5.justification: Both versions report results with ± values without specifying repeated-run counts or defining the uncertainty statistic. V2 adds no seed-count disclosure, confidence-interval procedure, or significance testing; changed uncertainty values and additional rows follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Every runtime entry in Tables 1–6 changes, while their coverage, average-width, and single-width/under-40-width entries remain identical. For example, Table 1's MOCP runtime changes from 14.12 ± 0.18 to 9.37 ± 0.05, without an explanation establishing the cause. Tables 7–10 and Figure 3 add substantial results; Table 11 repeats Table 2.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds Lemma 6 and a proof claiming an expected-set-size bound and a comparison with COMA. Section 3.2 revises per-iteration complexity from O(MNJ) to O(Nt + JMN). Theorems 1 and 3 remove their explicit initialization restriction, and Equations 33 and 44 correct M−1 to N−1, although the principal coverage and regret bounds are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: graph-based model selection and set-size feedback improve prediction-set efficiency, reduce computation, and provide coverage and sublinear-regret guarantees. The added appendix material does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: V2 discusses model-selection variability and shift severity as influences on coverage, and interprets local coverage as evidence of rapid adaptation (B.6–B.7). Appendix A.5 also infers that GMOCP's maximum set size is half COMA's; this interpretation exceeds what its stated expected-size bound establishes.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies 50,000 training samples, 6,000 test samples, and a separate 2,000-sample set for hyperparameter selection. V1 already specifies the 6,000-step evaluation horizon, so this is additional allocation information rather than evidence of a changed experiment. Hardware and existing hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Feldman et al. (2022), Bhatnagar et al. (2023), and Angelopoulos et al. (2024), supporting expanded online-prediction context and the new baselines. The central positioning relative to MOCP and COMA remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The title is revised, the introduction briefly expands its explanation of online conformal prediction, abbreviations are expanded, and terminology and citation style are edited. New appendix subsections organize the additions, but most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adopts TMLR typography, author formatting, running headers, and revised float placement throughout. It adds Tables 7–10 and Figure 3, redisplays Table 2 as Table 11, and moves the retained Figure 2 before the conclusion. Figures 1–2 retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The added single-model comparisons and robustness diagnostics address gaps in v1's empirical evaluation, and the sample-allocation disclosure improves reproducibility. However, runtime values throughout the retained tables change without explanation, and Appendix A.5 draws a maximum-size superiority claim from an expected-size bound that does not establish it. These benefits and new transparency and reasoning concerns leave the net quality improvement uncertain.
